correctness.rationale: Unique module coordinates give f∈tFq[t]/(t^m) and independent b,c∈Fq; characteristic polynomial forces nilpotence exactly when f(0)=d=0. Direct powers prove X² acts by f²+bc t^{m−1} and X^j by f^j for j≥3, so only valuations 2v=m−1 can exhibit quadratic cancellation. The rank computation separates v=m−1, all other nonzero f, and f=0. Counts L_v=(q−1)q^{m−v−1}, 2q−1 product-zero pairs, and q−1 prescribed-nonzero-product pairs exhaust all q^{m+1} nilpotent elements. The formula and its marginals follow by telescoping. Independent actual matrix enumeration corroborates 20 small cases; it is not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: A complete elementwise joint rank–index distribution with explicit coefficients for every field q and every m≥2 is not present in the materially inspected primary statements. Britnell–Wildon Prop.4.4 already classifies allowable partitions and uses the same centralizer coordinates; this support is not claimed as original. Oblak gives maximal indices, Sharma finite orbit counts, and Iarrobino et al. generic partitions. The finite-field coefficient refinement is additional, though possible older equivalent computations remain a real bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: The coordinates in Britnell–Wildon §4 could support a simple unprinted or later arithmetic derivation; absolute priority is not established.
A historical enumeration under Hall-polynomial, module endomorphism, or centralizer rank-zeta terminology could be equivalent.
The existing square-zero sublocus is covered separately; only the complete joint distribution and higher-index counts are proposed as new.

value.rationale: Ranks and nilpotency indices are canonical invariants of individual commuting nilpotent matrices, and their full joint distribution measures a natural arithmetic refinement of the well-developed Jordan-partition support problem. The formula applies in unbounded dimensions over every finite field, includes characteristic-sensitive socle cancellation with field-independent multiplicity, yields genuine gaps in the index support and an exact maximal-index density 1−q⁻¹ for every m≥3. It is more than a renaming or a single fixed small-parameter count; existing classification only determines possible orbit types, not numbers of elements by both invariants.
